entry.title: Is OurTime UK Worth It? An Honest Look for Over-50s

link.title: Is OurTime UK Worth It? An Honest Look for Over-50s

entry.content:
Short answer: OurTime UK is worth trying if you want a site where almost everyone is over 45 and you’re prepared to message people actively. Go in with your eyes open: you can’t send messages without paying, plans renew automatically, and its Trustpilot rating is 1.3 out of 5. Browse free first, and if you pay, start with the shortest plan and note your renewal date.

OurTime is a dating site for singles over 50, run in the UK by Match Group, the company behind Match.com.1 This guide covers who’s on it, what you get free and paid, what members complain about, and who should skip it.

Next step // Look before you payAffiliate link

Want to see who's near you? Joining and browsing is free. You only pay if you want to message.

Browse OurTime UK free

Affiliate link: if you sign up through it, Later Love UK may earn a commission. You pay the same either way. Disclosure.

Who uses OurTime UK

OurTime is aimed at people over 50, and its membership reflects that. DatingScout, which reviewed the UK site this month, puts the split at roughly 45% aged 45–54 and 55% aged 55 and over.2

The headline figure is about 2 million registered UK members, but that’s the site’s own claim. DatingScout’s estimate of people actually using it is far lower: around 100,000 active UK members, with about 175,000 using it in a typical week. The gender split leans male, at about 60% men to 40% women.

For a woman over 50, that ratio means plenty of interest. For a man, it means more competition, and it makes a good profile and photo more important.

What you get for free

OurTime’s help pages say a free account lets you create a profile, see a selection of profiles, and look at up to six singles in your search at a time.3 DatingScout adds that free members can like profiles and use Shuffle, which shows a stream of profiles to say yes or no to.

What free members can’t do is the part that matters: send messages. You also can’t see who has liked or viewed you.

What a subscription unlocks

According to OurTime, paying gets you:

  • unlimited messaging, and access to messages you’ve received
  • a list of who has liked and viewed your profile
  • the ability to go back to profiles you’ve seen
  • no adverts
  • advanced search filters and a few Super Likes a week, with the upgraded profile

Some extras cost more on top of a subscription, including profile Boosts and Private Mode.4 Current prices, and how to cancel, are in the cost and cancellation guide.

What members complain about

OurTime’s main Trustpilot page has a TrustScore of 1.3 out of 5 from more than 2,100 reviews, with 53% of them one-star.5 The complaints fall into a few clear groups:

  • Fake or inactive profiles. Members describe likes and views from people who never reply, or profiles that disappear.
  • Billing. Some say they were charged after they thought they’d cancelled.
  • Cancelling and deleting accounts. Several found it hard to cancel or to remove their profile.
  • Customer service. Many say emails and calls went unanswered.

Reviews are self-selected, and unhappy customers are more likely to write one. But the same themes appear again and again, so it’s worth planning around them rather than hoping you’ll be the exception.

The billing complaints, explained

OurTime’s own help pages explain the most common billing surprise. Suspending your profile does not cancel your subscription, so it keeps renewing until you cancel the renewal itself.6 The cancellation guide walks through the right steps for the website, iPhone and Android.

Safety features

OurTime lets you report any profile, or anyone in your messages, from the three-dot menu, and its moderation team can remove members.7 You can also earn a Verified badge by uploading a selfie, which is worth doing yourself and looking for in others.

No site can screen out every bad actor. Before you message anyone, read the romance scam warning signs. People aged 55 to 74 lose more to romance fraud than any other age group.

Who it suits, and who should skip it

It may suit you if:

  • you want to meet people your own age, without younger users in the mix
  • you’re comfortable messaging first rather than waiting to be contacted
  • you’ll use it steadily for a month or two, then decide

Skip it, or wait, if:

  • you’d rather not pay before you can say hello. Match lets free members talk to people who’ve paid for a feature called Connect. See the comparison of OurTime, eharmony and Match.
  • you know you’ll forget to cancel. Set a reminder for three days before renewal the moment you subscribe.
Next step // Try it freeAffiliate link

Decided it's worth a look? Make a free profile first and see who's near you before paying anything.

Try OurTime UK free

Questions people ask

Is OurTime UK free?

You can join, make a profile and browse a limited selection for free. Messaging, reading messages, and seeing who liked or viewed you all need a subscription.

Who owns OurTime UK?

Match Group, which also owns Match.com.

Does OurTime UK have fake profiles?

Many reviewers say so. OurTime checks profiles and photos and offers a selfie Verified badge, but fake or inactive profiles are the most common complaint.

Does OurTime renew automatically?

Yes. Cancel the renewal no later than 48 hours before the renewal date, or you’ll be charged for another term.

entry.title: OurTime UK Cost in 2026, and How to Cancel

link.title: OurTime UK Cost in 2026, and How to Cancel

entry.content:
Short answer: as of October 2026, OurTime UK costs £39.99 for one month, £74.97 for three months (£24.99 a month) or £119.94 for six months (£19.99 a month).1 Every plan renews automatically. To stop it, cancel the renewal at least 48 hours before your renewal date, in the same place you paid: the website, the App Store, or Google Play.

Prices on dating sites change and are sometimes discounted at checkout, so always check the figure on the payment screen before you confirm.

OurTime UK prices

Plan Per month Total you pay
1 month £39.99 £39.99
3 months £24.99 £74.97
6 months £19.99 £119.94

Extras that cost more

On top of a subscription, OurTime sells optional extras:2

  • Incognito mode: £1.99 a day, or £9.99 for a month
  • Boosts, which push your profile up the list: from £1.99 for one
  • Love Notes: from £7.99 for five

None of these are needed to message people. They’re the most common way the cost creeps up, so decide your budget before you start.

The cheapest way to try it

This is where the plan prices hide a trap and a saving.

  • If you’ll use it for just one month, the one-month plan at £39.99 is the cheapest option.
  • If you might use it for two months, the three-month plan (£74.97) costs less than paying for one month twice (£79.98), and gives you a spare month.
  • If you’re committed for three months or more, the six-month plan works out at half the monthly price of the one-month plan.

A sensible route is to browse free first, which costs nothing.3 If you then like who you’re seeing nearby, pay for one month, and decide in week three whether to carry on.

Next step // Start freeAffiliate link

Not sure yet? A free profile shows you who's near you before you spend anything.

Make a free OurTime profile

Affiliate link: if you sign up through it, Later Love UK may earn a commission. You pay the same either way. Disclosure.

How to cancel OurTime UK

Cancel in the same place you paid. OurTime’s help pages give these routes:4

On a computer

  1. Log in and open your account settings.
  2. Go to Manage account, then Manage subscription.
  3. Cancel the automatic renewal and follow it through to the end.

On a phone (mobile site or Android app)

  1. Go to your profile, then Settings.
  2. Scroll to Preferences and choose Cancel your pass.
  3. Complete the cancellation.

If you paid through Google Play, open the Play Store, tap your profile, then Payments & subscriptions, then Subscriptions, and cancel OurTime there.

If you paid through an iPhone, open the iPhone’s Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions, and cancel OurTime there.

Get the timing right

OurTime says you can cancel no earlier than 24 hours after you buy and no later than 48 hours before the renewal date. Miss that window and you’ll pay for another full term.

The day you subscribe, put a reminder in your phone or calendar for three days before the renewal date.

Why some people are still charged after cancelling

OurTime’s own help page lists the usual reasons:5

  • You suspended your profile instead of cancelling. Suspending hides you but doesn’t stop the subscription renewing. This is the most common mix-up.
  • The cancellation didn’t finish. If you didn’t get a confirmation email, it may not have gone through.
  • You have a second profile with its own subscription.
  • You bought extras that are billed separately.
  • You paid in instalments, in which case payments can still be due after you cancel.

If you’re charged after cancelling properly, keep your confirmation email and contact OurTime’s customer service. If that doesn’t resolve it, ask your bank or card provider about disputing the payment.

Refunds

DatingScout reports that OurTime UK offers a 14-day money-back guarantee.6 OurTime’s own help pages don’t spell out the terms, so if you change your mind soon after paying, contact customer service straight away and ask in writing.

How it compares on price

OurTime’s six-month price is mid-range for over-50s dating. Match’s six-month plan was much cheaper in the same October 2026 price checks, while eharmony’s shortest plan is six months and costs more. The comparison of OurTime, eharmony and Match puts them side by side.

Questions people ask

How much is OurTime UK per month?

£39.99 for a single month, £24.99 a month on the three-month plan, or £19.99 a month on the six-month plan, as of October 2026.

How do I cancel OurTime UK?

In account settings, then Manage account, then Manage subscription. If you paid through the App Store or Google Play, cancel in that store instead.

When do I need to cancel by?

No later than 48 hours before your renewal date.

Why am I still being charged after cancelling?

Usually because the profile was suspended rather than the renewal cancelled. Suspending doesn’t stop payments.

entry.title: OurTime vs eharmony vs Match for Over-50s (UK)

link.title: OurTime vs eharmony vs Match for Over-50s (UK)

entry.content:
Short answer: choose OurTime if you want a site where nearly everyone is over 45. Choose Match for the biggest UK membership and the cheapest six-month plan. Choose eharmony if you want guided matching for a long-term relationship and can commit to six months or more. None of them lets you message freely without paying.

All prices below are from DatingScout’s UK price checks in October 2026.1 Prices change and checkout offers vary, so confirm on the site before you pay.

Disclosure // Before you readAffiliate link

This site has an affiliate link for OurTime only, not for eharmony or Match. That hasn't changed anything in this comparison.

Visit OurTime UK

Affiliate link: if you sign up through it, Later Love UK may earn a commission. You pay the same either way. Disclosure.

Side by side

  OurTime UK eharmony UK Match UK
Built for Over-50s All ages All ages
UK members (claimed) about 2,000,000 about 600,000 about 780,000
Shortest plan 1 month, £39.99 6 months, £239.40 1 month, £29.99
Six-month total £119.94 £239.40 £59.94
Message for free? No No Only with members using Connect
Auto-renews? Yes Yes Yes

Membership numbers are each site’s own claims, as reported by DatingScout, and they count everyone who ever registered.2 Active members are far fewer on every site.

OurTime: built for over-50s

OurTime’s selling point is simple: you’re not wading through profiles of people decades younger. DatingScout estimates about 55% of its UK members are 55 or over, and the rest mostly 45 to 54.

The downsides are well documented. Its main Trustpilot page scores 1.3 out of 5, with complaints about inactive profiles and billing. It’s also the only one of the three with a monthly price above £30. The full OurTime review covers who it suits.

Match: biggest and cheapest over six months

Match has the most claimed UK members of the general sites here, and its six-month plan works out at £9.99 a month, the lowest in this comparison.3

Free members can create a profile, search and send likes, and can talk to members who’ve paid for Connect. The catch is that Match is for all ages, so you’ll set your age filters and see a wider mix. It’s also owned by Match Group, the same company as OurTime.

eharmony: guided matching, longer commitment

eharmony matches people on a detailed compatibility questionnaire rather than leaving you to browse, and it’s aimed at long-term relationships. DatingScout reports a slightly female-leaning membership, about 53% women.

Its plans start at six months, so it has the highest upfront cost here, although longer plans bring the monthly price down.4 Free members can’t see photos or message freely.

Which should you pick?

  • You want people your own age and you’ll message first: OurTime.
  • You’re watching the cost: Match’s six-month plan.
  • You want a serious, long-term match and don’t mind the commitment: eharmony.
  • You’re not sure: make free profiles on two of them. A free profile costs nothing, and seeing who’s actually near you is the best test.

Whichever you choose, read the romance scam warning signs before you start messaging, and note your renewal date the day you pay.

Questions people ask

Which dating site is best for over-50s in the UK?

OurTime if you want only people around your age, Match for size and price, and eharmony for guided matching towards a long-term relationship.

Which is cheapest?

Match’s six-month plan, at £59.94 in October 2026 price checks.

Can you message for free on any of them?

Not freely. On Match, free members can message people who have paid for Connect.

entry.title: Romance Scams After 50: Warning Signs and What to Do

link.title: Romance Scams After 50: Warning Signs and What to Do

entry.content:
Short answer: the clearest warning sign is being asked for money by someone you’ve only met online, for any reason. Others are moving fast to declarations of love, wanting to leave the dating site for private messages, always having a reason not to meet or video call, and asking you to keep the relationship secret. If any of this is happening, stop sending money, tell someone you trust, and report it.

This guide has no affiliate links. It’s here because romance fraud hits people over 50 hardest, and knowing the pattern is the best protection.

How big the problem is

Report Fraud, the UK’s national fraud reporting service, says romance fraud cost victims more than £102 million last year, from 10,784 reports, a 29% rise on the year before.1

The losses fall hardest on people in later life. People aged 55 to 74 lost the most, nearly half of the total. The average victim lost about £9,500, and some lost up to £1 million.

Romance scammers are organised and patient. They often build trust over weeks or months before money is mentioned, and the request usually comes wrapped in an emotional story, so the warning signs below matter more than how careful you think you are.

The warning signs

Police and Get Safe Online, the UK’s public online-safety service, point to the same pattern.2

They ask for money

This is the one that matters most. It might be a medical emergency, a business problem, a fee to release an inheritance, travel costs to come and see you, or an “investment” they want to share with you. Never send money or bank details to someone you’ve only met online, however convincing the reason and however long you’ve been talking.

Things move very fast

Strong declarations of love within days or weeks, talk of a future together before you’ve met, and lots of attention and flattery. Taking things slowly is a safety measure, not a sign of coldness.

They want to leave the dating site

Scammers often ask to move to WhatsApp, text or email early on. Staying on the dating site’s messaging keeps you inside its reporting and moderation tools.3

They can’t meet or video call

Someone who’s always abroad, working on an oil rig, serving overseas or just about to visit, but never quite does, and whose camera is always broken. Be particularly wary of people who say they’re local but turn out to be overseas.

They want secrecy

Asking you not to tell friends or family about them is a classic way to isolate you from people who’d spot the problem.

Their photos or story don’t add up

Pictures that look professional or too perfect, or details that change. Search their name and phrases from their messages along with words like “romance scam”, and run a reverse image search on their photos. Scammers often use pictures stolen from someone else.

Protect yourself before you start

  • Use a reputable dating site and keep messages on it until you’re sure the person is genuine.
  • Keep personal details back: your full name, date of birth, home address, workplace, and family details.
  • Talk about who you’re meeting with a friend or family member. A second opinion is the most effective protection there is.
  • Meet in person, in a public place, sooner rather than later. Someone who keeps avoiding meeting is a warning in itself. The first date safety checklist covers how.

If you think it’s happening to you

  1. Stop sending money straight away, however much it hurts to do so.
  2. Call your bank using the number on the back of your card, and tell them what’s happened. Do it quickly; the sooner they know, the better the chance of stopping payments.
  3. Report it. In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, report to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or on 0300 123 2040. In Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101.4
  4. Report the profile to the dating site, so they can remove it and protect others.
  5. Keep everything: messages, photos, payment records and usernames.
  6. Talk to someone. Victims often feel ashamed, and scammers rely on that. These are organised criminals who do this for a living. Being targeted says nothing about your judgement.

If someone threatens you or you feel in danger, call 999.

Questions people ask

What is the biggest sign of a romance scam?

Being asked for money by someone you’ve only met online, whatever the reason.

Who do I report a romance scam to?

Report Fraud (reportfraud.police.uk, 0300 123 2040) in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, or Police Scotland on 101. Tell your bank and the dating site too.

Are over-50s more likely to be targeted?

People aged 55 to 74 suffered the highest losses last year, nearly half of the £102 million total.

Sources

  • Romance fraud costs UK victims £102 million, Report Fraud
  • Report Fraud service goes live, City of London Police
  • Top tips to avoid romance scams, Action Fraud
  • DateSafe leaflet, Get Safe Online, via Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner
  • How can I keep myself safe on the site?, OurTime UK

  1. Figures released by City of London Police through Report Fraud, comparing with 2024. ↩

  2. From Get Safe Online’s DateSafe advice and Action Fraud’s romance scam tips. ↩

  3. OurTime, for example, advises members to stay on the platform while getting to know someone. ↩

  4. Report Fraud replaced Action Fraud as the national reporting service in December 2025. ↩

entry.title: First Date Safety After 50: A Practical Checklist

link.title: First Date Safety After 50: A Practical Checklist

entry.content:
Short answer: meet somewhere public and busy, get there and back under your own steam, and tell someone where you’re going and when you’ll check in. Keep your phone charged, keep the first date short, and don’t share your home address until you’re sure. If you feel uncomfortable in a pub or bar, ask staff for “Angela” and they’ll help you leave.

This guide has no affiliate links. The advice comes from police, Get Safe Online and the dating sites’ own safety pages.1

Before the date

  • Check they’re real. A short video call before you meet is the simplest test. If they keep finding reasons not to, treat it as a warning. The romance scam guide explains why.
  • Do a quick search. Look up their name, and run a reverse image search on their photos to make sure they aren’t someone else’s.
  • Tell a friend or family member who you’re meeting, where, and when. Share the person’s profile name and a photo.
  • Agree a check-in time, and a code word that means “call me with an excuse to leave”.
  • Charge your phone and turn on location sharing with your trusted person for the evening if you’re comfortable doing so.

Choosing the place

  • Public and busy: a café, a pub at lunchtime, a garden centre, a museum.
  • Somewhere you know, close to your own transport, not theirs.
  • Daytime is easier. It’s natural to keep a coffee to an hour, and it gives you both an easy way to say “let’s do this again”.
  • Avoid their home or yours until you know them well.

During the date

  • Get yourself there and home. Don’t accept a lift on a first date, and don’t let them see where you live.
  • Keep an eye on your drink, and don’t leave it unattended.
  • Keep personal details back: your address, workplace, finances and family details can wait.
  • Trust your instincts. You can leave at any point, for any reason, without explaining.

Ask for Angela

Many pubs, bars and venues take part in Ask for Angela. If you feel unsafe or uncomfortable on a date, go to the bar and ask for “Angela”. Staff will help you discreetly, for example by moving you somewhere out of sight, calling you a taxi, or asking the other person to leave. If you’re at risk, they’ll call the police.2

If you’re ever in immediate danger, call 999.

After the date

  • Message your check-in person to say you’re home safe.
  • Take your time. Someone pressing for a quick second date at your home, or for money, is a red flag.
  • Report anyone who made you feel unsafe to the dating site, so they can act, and to the police if they threatened or hurt you.

Checking a partner’s history: Clare’s Law

As a relationship develops, you have a right to ask. In England and Wales, the Domestic Violence Disclosure Scheme, known as Clare’s Law, lets you ask the police whether a new or current partner has a history of domestic abuse or violence.3 Friends and family can also apply if they’re worried about you.

The police check their records, and a local panel decides what can safely be shared. Anything disclosed is confidential. If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 999 rather than waiting.

Questions people ask

Where should I go on a first date?

Somewhere public and busy that you can reach and leave on your own, such as a café or a pub at lunchtime.

What is Ask for Angela?

A scheme in many pubs and bars: ask staff for “Angela” if you feel unsafe on a date, and they’ll help you leave discreetly.

Can I check if a new partner has a history of abuse?

Yes. In England and Wales, Clare’s Law lets you ask the police.

Sources

  • DateSafe leaflet, Get Safe Online, via Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner
  • Lancashire Police’s safe dating tips, Blackpool Gazette
  • How can I keep myself safe on the site?, OurTime UK
  • Ask for Angela, Wiltshire Council
  • Clare’s Law, Sussex Police

  1. Mainly Get Safe Online’s DateSafe advice, Lancashire Police’s dating tips, and OurTime UK’s safety page. ↩

  2. How it works, as described by Wiltshire Council for venues across Wiltshire and Swindon. ↩

  3. Created in 2014 after Clare Wood was killed by a former partner. To apply, contact your local police force; many forces take applications online. ↩
entry.summary: A first date after 50 should feel exciting, not risky. A practical checklist for before, during and after, plus Ask for Angela and Clare's Law.
